title: Lifting a covering of a closed fibre
statement:
Let $W$ be affine, let $Z_W\subset W$ be closed, and assume $W\setminus Z_W$
is quasi-compact. A finite affine ind-etale covering $\{V_a\to Z_W\}$
extends to a finite pro-etale covering of $W$ whose members over the closed
fibre are $v_W(V_a)$, and whose other members are affine opens in
$W\setminus Z_W$. Their reductions to $Z_W$ are respectively $V_a$ and
empty.

proof.text: Choose $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$. By the affine description of a closed immersion, $Z_W=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ for an ideal $J\subseteq B$, with underlying set $V(J)=\{\mathfrak p:J\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$. Thus $W\setminus Z_W=\bigcup_{f\in J}D(f)$: a prime outside $V(J)$ omits an element of $J$, and a prime in $D(f)$ with $f\in J$ cannot contain $J$. These sets are open by the basic-open spectrum lemma. The assumed quasi-compactness, whose definition is the finite-subcover property, therefore selects finitely many $f_b\in J$ with $W\setminus Z_W=\bigcup_bD(f_b)$. An empty complement permits an empty list.

source.place: Proof, first two sentences; affine closed immersion: Stacks 01QO; basic opens: 00E0

proof.text: For each $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}\overline C_a$ in the given finite covering, form $L_a=v_W(V_a)=\operatorname{Spec}H_B(\overline C_a)$ by the closed-site lift. The construction takes values in $\mathcal B_W$, whose objects are affine ind-etale objects of the small pro-etale site; hence each $L_a$ is affine and ind-etale over $W$. The cited ind-etale stability theorem explicitly says that an ind-etale map is weakly etale, so $L_a\to W$ is weakly etale. By the affine fibre-product formula and the quotient tensor formula, its closed base change is $L_a\times_W Z_W=\operatorname{Spec}(H_B(\overline C_a)/JH_B(\overline C_a))$. The specified reduction map is an isomorphism by the closed-lift reduction lemma. Applying the contravariant spectrum functor of the affine-spectrum definition identifies this base change with $V_a$ over $Z_W$, and its map into $L_a$ is the quotient-induced closed immersion. The hypothesis of the reduction lemma holds because $\overline C_a$ is ind-etale over $B/J$.

source.place: Proof, lift and reduction sentences; Stacks 097P (lemma-lift-ind-etale) and 09BK (lemma-closed-immersion-affines); affine base change: 01I4/01JQ and 00DF

proof.text: For every selected $f_b$, let $O_b=\operatorname{Spec}B_{f_b}$. The principal-localization open-immersion lemma identifies $O_b\to W$ with the inclusion of the affine open $D(f_b)$. An open immersion is weakly etale directly from the definitions: its local-ring maps are isomorphisms, hence flat, and its diagonal identifies the open subscheme with its self fibre product, by the fibre-product universal property: the two projections coincide on the open subscheme, and the diagonal is inverse to either projection. Its diagonal local-ring maps are therefore also isomorphisms. An isomorphism of rings is flat since tensoring along it is the identity after identifying the rings. Thus both flatness clauses hold. The same affine base-change formulas as in Step 2 identify its reduction ring with $B_{f_b}/JB_{f_b}$. The image of $f_b$ is a unit by the localization definition and belongs to $JB_{f_b}$ because $f_b\in J$. Consequently $1\in JB_{f_b}$, the quotient ring is zero, and its spectrum is empty.

source.place: Proof, complementary affine opens and empty reduction; Stacks 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine), with the flatness and quotient arguments written out

proof.text: The combined family $\{L_a\to W\}_a\cup\{O_b\to W\}_b$ is finite and jointly surjective. Indeed, a point of $Z_W$ has a preimage in some $V_a$ by the covering hypothesis. Composing that point with $V_a\cong L_a\times_W Z_W\to L_a$ from Step 2 gives a point of $L_a$ with the original image in $W$. A point outside $Z_W$ lies in some $D(f_b)$ by Step 1 and hence has a preimage in $O_b$ by Step 3. This proves joint surjectivity without any assertion that images of weakly etale maps are open.

source.place: Proof, images of the lifts cover the closed subset and the basic opens cover its complement

proof.text: Verify the full covering condition, not just surjectivity. Each member $T\to W$ of the combined family has affine source and affine target, so the affine-morphism lemma makes the preimage $T_E=T\times_W E$ of every affine open $E\subseteq W$ an affine open of $T$. The finite family of these affine opens has images whose union is $E$, by Step 4. Together with the weak etaleness checked in Steps 2 and 3, this is exactly the definition of a pro-etale covering. Steps 2 and 3 give respectively its specified closed reductions $V_a$ and the empty scheme, so all the required clauses hold.

source.place: Proof, final covering conclusion, with the fpqc condition checked on every affine open; Stacks 0989 (definition-fpqc-covering)

proof_origin.place: Proof paragraph, expanded using Stacks 097P and 09BK for the existing lift and 0989 for the covering condition

lean.statement:
theorem exists_ofArrows_closedLiftCover_mem_proetalePrecoverage
    (hJ : IsCompact (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set B))ᶜ) [Finite ι]
    [∀ a, Algebra.IndEtale (B ⧸ J) (C a)]
    (hC : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum (B ⧸ J), ∃ a,
      p ∈ Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap (B ⧸ J) (C a)))) :
    ∃ (κ : Type u) (_ : Finite κ) (f : κ → B), (∀ b, f b ∈ J) ∧
      (⋃ b, (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (f b) : Set (PrimeSpectrum B))) =
        (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set B))ᶜ ∧
      Presieve.ofArrows _ (closedLiftCoverHom C f) ∈ Scheme.proetalePrecoverage (Spec (.of B)) ∧
      (∀ a, Function.Bijective (Algebra.ClosedLift.reduction B (C a) J)) ∧
      ∀ b, Subsingleton
        (Localization.Away (f b) ⧸ J.map (algebraMap B (Localization.Away (f b))))
lean.note: The existing upstream theorem explicitly names this blueprint node. It states the finite covering extension in affine coordinates W = Spec B and Z_W = Spec(B/J). The input finite affine ind-etale covering is encoded by ind-etale quotient algebras and joint surjectivity on prime spectra (equivalent here to the full pro-etale covering condition). The output uses the same Algebra.ClosedLift as the recorded closedSiteLift, together with principal affine opens in the complement; it includes the full proetalePrecoverage condition, bijectivity of the specified closed reduction maps, and zero complementary reduction rings.
